newsitem.title: UK: Med Urals value disputed, but buyers seen relaxed.
newsitem.headline: Med Urals value disputed, but buyers seen relaxed.

text.p: Mediterranean crude traders were still at odds over the value of Urals on Thursday, but the majority seemed to agree that prices would settle at the lower end of their recent trading range.
Two small Urals cargoes traded earlier in the week at Dated Brent -12.5 cents and Dated Brent -30 cents CIF.

While bad weather and the closure of berth one at Novorossiisk has crimped supplies, the major refinery buyers said they were relaxed as they anticipated the arrival of Iraqi Kirkuk crude onto the market.
A seller with an 80,000 tonne cargo scheduled to load on December 25 said he was offering it in the (Dated Brent minus) 20 cents bracket.
West African markets were quiet with distillate-rich grades expected to come under pressure from recent weakness in heating oil.
"With that plus Iraq coming back things could soften a bit," said one trader.
Nevertheless, traders said there were still some transatlantic arbitrage opportunities.
"The arb is only half working...The East Coast (U.S.) refineries are still interested but I don't know about the Gulf Coast."
In the other direction, a total of six VLCCs of West African crude, between a quarter and a third of the December programme, was sold into Far East markets this month, traders said.

A third decade Jan Bonny Medium/Bonny Light combination cargo was sold into the Med on Tuesday at Dated Brent +62/63 cents, and there were rumours that another earlier-loading combo cargo was sold into Spain at around the same price.
"It is not what I would call a strong market by any means," said one dealer.
